notes: Fix: the catalogue's arduino-mkr1000 entry lists only USB, VIN, VCC, GND and BAT, so it has no port '2' for the pin the tutorial wires the LED to. lookup_part returned the same five ports. I made a new type, arduino-mkr1000-wifi, with the full header from the circuit image: 0-14, A0-A6, AREF, 5V, VIN, VCC, GND, RESET, plus BAT and USB. mkr1 now uses it. Pin 8 is not labelled in the image but is on the real board, so I included it.
The parts are otherwise unchanged from step 1.
Circuit: MKR pin 2 -> green wire -> 220 ohm resistor -> LED anode; LED cathode -> black wire -> GND. The resistor is on the anode side, as in the image and schematic.

Breadboard holes follow the catalogue naming (bank 'b' = rows f-j, drawn on top in the image). The green wire and resistor leg 1 are in column 3, resistor leg 2 and the LED anode (bent leg) in column 6, and the LED cathode and black wire in column 8. Row letters within a column are approximate; any row in the same strip is equivalent.

The LED is driven from a 3.3 V logic pin through 220 ohm, which is within the board's limits. The sketch itself uses LED_BUILTIN, but the tutorial text says the external LED is on pin 2, so I followed the circuit image.
